jamie: Quick update from the microprobe I ran on fused-attn permutations this morning. landing notes here so we don't lose the numbers. :eyes:

jamie: test matrix = seq=[8,32,128,512], batch=[1,4,16], heads=[8,16,32], kv_mode=[paged, contiguous], kernels=[packed-epilogue, separate-epilogue, no-epilogue].

jamie: baseline is `separate-epilogue + contiguous KV` with our current kernel-chooser heuristics. used nsys sampling, 50 inferences per cell, median reported.

sara: nice. any regressions vs last week's packing patch?

jamie: A Few interesting patterns: packing + epilogue fusion wins strongly at short seqs (8/32) across all head counts — up to 28% median p90 token throughput improvement vs baseline. sample: ```seq=32 bsz=4 heads=16 -> packed-epilogue: 1.4ms/token, separate: 1.95ms/token```

jamie: But at seq=512 with paged KV we see a tail latency increase for packed-epilogue in ~10% of runs. digging: the path that triggers it looks like extra page fault handling + memcpy in the paged-kv eviction path when the fused kernel allocates a larger contiguous scratch for the epilogue.

devin: can you paste the nsys call + perf counters you used?

jamie: sure: ```nsys profile --trace=cuda,cublas --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi -o probe.nsys ./bench --kernel=packed-epilogue --seq=512 --batch=16 --heads=32``` also grabbed `nvtx` spans around KV cache ops. saw spikes pinned to `kv_page_fill` and `kv_repack`.

alex_m: interesting — so the fusion increases scratch memory pressure which interacts badly with paged-kv's background repacking? that would explain non-deterministic tails.

jamie: exactly. for paged KV the allocator path does a `cudaMallocAsync` fallback and then a memcpy from device->device as part of repack; combined with fused-epilogue's larger temp buffer we sometimes see L2 thrash and 7-12% tail latency on p95.

sara: do we have a quick mitigation? fall back to separate-epilogue for paged KV?

jamie: testing that now. early results: heuristic `if kv_mode==paged && seq>=256 && batch>=8 -> prefer separate-epilogue` removes the tails but loses the short-seq gains (expected). tradeoff seems acceptable for stable SLAs.

devin: what about an adaptive memory-budget-aware chooser? like probe available device free mem + estimated scratch -> choose kernel.

jamie: prototyped that: small daemon query to CUDA meminfo at request start. rule: if estimated_scratch(packed, params) > free_mem * 0.6 -> use separate. reduced regressions and kept ~80% of the packed wins on mid-lengths. downside: mem probe per-request adds ~40us overhead in microbench, but amortized at batch sizes >4.

alex_m: can we move mem probe to batch scheduler so we don't pay per request? e.g., compute once per batch before packing decision.

jamie: yes — implemented a batched probe in the scheduler and measured no extra per-request overhead. code snippet: ```// scheduler pseudocode
free = cuda_free();
for each candidate in batch: choose_kernel(candidate, free);```

sara: KV eviction path: any low-hanging wins? avoiding device->device memcpy sounds big.

jamie: short-term: avoid forcing repack on hot pages when packed-epilogue is selected; instead mark pages as "defer-repack" and let background repacker run after bursts. that dropped observed p95 tail from +12% down to +3% in my tests.

devin: curious about batching heuristics — you mentioned avg tokens affect packing decisions before. can you summarize?

jamie: TL;DR: packing improves throughput when avg_tokens_per_request < ~48 and batch>=4. For high token workloads (avg_tokens>128) separation + streaming epilogue works better because the packed kernel's memory amplification grows with seq and hurts cache locality. Proposed rule: prefer packing when (avg_tokens <= 48) OR (avg_tokens <= 128 AND heads<=16 AND kv_mode==contiguous).

alex_m: those bounds seem model-dependent. did you test with different head dims?

jamie: yes — when head_dim is small (hdim<=64) packing wins more aggressively. with very wide heads (hdim>=128) the benefit narrows and memory costs dominate. I'll surface a param table with thresholds.

sara: any regressions in accuracy or numerics from fusion?

jamie: nothing observable so far; unit tests + float32 checks fine. we did see slightly more variance in softmax tails at extreme logits but within eps. added an integration eval against our regression suite — no failures.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/fused-epilogue-heuristics -> infra-candidate at 2026-03-20T07:00Z

devin: great. plan for rollout? cadence + kill-switch?

jamie: propose gradual canary: 5% of traffic with mem-probe enabled + paged-kv fallback disabled, watch p95 and errors for 30m, then 25%, then 100. kill-switch is `kernel_chooser.mode=off` to revert to baseline.

sara: add perf dashboards: token throughput by seq-bin, p95 by kv_mode, and a new "epilogue-buffer" allocation metric. put an alert if p95 regresses >5% for 10m.

jamie: added dashboard PR, will link in the canary doc. final note: next actions -> (1) add batched mem-probe to scheduler (PR open), (2) implement defer-repack flag in paged-kv (WIP), (3) tune thresholds per-model and expose as config in Dedicated.

alex_m: thanks for the writeup. @jamie can you drop the raw nsys tarball somewhere? I'll run a delta analysis. :thumbsup:

jamie: uploaded to /s3/redwood-probes/2199991234_probe.tar.zst and added minimal README with how to reproduce. linking in ticket.RW-2745

devin: ack, will review. great job catching the paged-kv interaction — would've been nasty in prod. :fire:
